implementations.name: CookingFrame
implementations.moduleDoc:
CookingFrame — the web cooking surface: full screen, outside AppShell, because cooking is a
focused task.

One centred column at every band: the top bar pinned at the top, the foot pinned at the bottom (the
Next preview above the actions), and only the body between them scrolls, so a focus line taller than the screen at
the largest text never pushes the place or Back / Next away. The foot keeps a gap above it, so a line cut off at the
bottom of the body reads as more to scroll. The surface is a size container, for the under-360 width rules and the
short-screen height rule, and is busy while the recipe loads.

The route's offline notice (`CookingNoticeSlot`) is the first thing in the centred column, above the top bar and
starting where it starts.

Presentational: props → JSX, plus the notice slot it reads from context.

The whole row is the control: a `button` with `role="checkbox"`, named by the line's text, at least 44 px tall, as

implementations.name: CookingLineRow
implementations.moduleDoc:
CookingLineRow — one line of a cooking step on native: the whole row is ONE checkbox, named by the
line's own text, at least the platform touch floor tall, with the box drawn by the design system's glyph, which owns its slot and its size
by the role of the line, so the box sits on the first line however the text wraps.

The press is the house `PressScale` with the checkbox role and its checked state, so a held row shrinks like every other
house control and a screen reader says "checked" or "not checked". The row is not given a name: its text is the name,
so stating it again would be a second stop saying the same thing.

The focus line is set in the role named by `LINE_TYPE.focus`, the one seam both platforms read, and every other line in
`readingBody`.

Presentational: props → JSX, apart from taking the screen-reader cursor when the screen asks (`focusRequested`).

implementations.name: CookingNav
implementations.moduleDoc:
CookingNav — the web Back / forward pair at the foot of the cooking column.

Two equal halves of one row, both the house `Button size="lg"` (52). Back is first and forward is last in reading
order, so forward sits on the reach side. Forward is quiet (the neutral secondary surface) until it is the action
now ("Start step n", "Finish" once every line is ticked); the screen says which with `tone`. Under 360
wide the chevrons hide and the labels stay whole.

Presentational: props → JSX.

implementations.name: CookingNoticeSlot
implementations.moduleDoc:
CookingNoticeSlot — the one place on the web cooking surface where the route's offline notice is drawn.

Cooking mode's package does not import `@commise/query`, so it cannot mount the notice itself. The route (which does)
hands the notice in through this slot, and `CookingFrame`, the one frame every cooking screen draws, puts it first in
the surface, above the top bar, with no prop threaded through the screens. Without a provider the slot is empty.

Orchestration: it supplies a value to its subtree and draws no markup of its own.

implementations.name: CookingScreen
implementations.moduleDoc:
CookingScreen — the web cooking screen: the read-level orchestration of cooking mode. It decides which screen to draw before
a session exists (`useCookingEntry`: loading, error, gone, no steps) and mounts `CookingSessionScreen` only once the
recipe is ready to cook. Where to go (the recipe, the editor, Home) is the route adapter's: it hands callbacks in.

Because the session is mounted below this switch and keyed by the recipe, the read always wins at the join: a read
that goes back to loading, or arrives with no steps, replaces Done rather than sitting under it.

implementations.name: CookingSessionScreen
implementations.moduleDoc:
CookingSessionScreen — the session-level orchestration of web cooking mode: the steps and Done. Mounted by
`CookingScreen` only once the recipe has steps to cook, so the session never opens on an empty recipe. The model is
`useCookingSessionScreen`'s; this screen draws it and adds the web's own behaviour: the ← / → keys, the swipe, the
polite announcement of a step change, and moving focus to Done's title. The read-level states (loading, error, gone, no
steps) are `CookingScreen`'s, so the read always wins over the session.

CookingStep — the web cooking step body.

Top to bottom: the step track, the record of ticked lines behind a Show disclosure, the line count, the focus line, the

focus, and every string, are decided by the screen.

CookingStep — a cooking step's body on native: a region named by the place, holding the step
track, the collapsed record of ticked lines with Show, the "Line n of N" overline (absent for a one-line step), the
focus line, the "Then" lines, and, once every line is ticked, Up next (the next step's first line at the focus size,

Which line is the focus and which are ticked is decided by the screen from cooking-core's line ticks; this leaf draws
what it is handed and reports presses. The track is decoration: the place in the top bar says the same thing, so it is
hidden from assistive tech. Up next is read-only text, never a control.

implementations.name: CookingTopBar
implementations.moduleDoc:
CookingTopBar — the web cooking top bar.

Exit, then the place, then, while the screen gives `ingredients`, the quiet Ingredients button with its `listChecks`
glyph and its label whole. Exit is ONE quiet `md` control, the × and the word together, with one accessible name.
The place is plain text. The bar is one tree in the order Exit, Ingredients, place: under 360 wide the place drops
to its own full-width row under Exit and Ingredients, which stay side by side while they fit, and the Exit label
stays. Wide, an `order` class moves Ingredients after the place, so the place takes the free space.

Presentational: props → JSX.

implementations.name: CookingTopBar
implementations.moduleDoc:
CookingTopBar — the native top bar: Exit as ONE control, the × and its visible label together with one
accessible name, on the quiet `md` house Button (44, lifted to the platform touch floor), then the place as plain
text, then, while the screen gives `ingredients`, the quiet Ingredients button with its `listChecks` glyph and its
label whole. Done passes no place, so it shows Exit alone. The bar wraps by whole controls, so no label wraps inside
its button or is cut. Wide, the order is Exit, the place, Ingredients. Narrow (under 360), the place takes its own
row under Exit and Ingredients, which stay side by side while they fit and wrap whole when they do not.
Ingredients sits at the end of the bar: wide, the place takes the free space; narrow, it has an auto start margin.

Props are the shared contract's `CookingTopBarProps` plus native's `narrow`, which the screen reads from the window
once, because a leaf never reads the device: web's container query does the same work, so the web leaf has no such
prop.

implementations.moduleDoc:
CookingTwoColumnLayout — the native two-column layout at L2 and L3: the ingredients column in a 300 wide slot
on the left that scrolls on its own, and the step column in the rest, at most 680 wide and centred in it. The slot is
on the canvas with no divider, and its content is inset 16 on every side inside the scroll, as the house sheet's
edge is, so the scroll bar stays at the slot edge. It holds no state and reads no band: the screen picks it by
`layoutBand`.

Presentational: props → JSX.

implementations.name: CookingIngredientsList
implementations.moduleDoc:
CookingIngredientsList — the cooking ingredients list on web: the servings stepper, the lines under their
section labels and Clear ticks. Every piece is the recipe page's own (`IngredientRuns`, `ServingScaleControl`,
through `@commise/features-recipes/cook`), so cooking mode groups, names and keys a line, sets an amount and counts
servings exactly as the page does, in the page's own words.

It holds no state, no frame and no heading: the sheet and the column wrap it and draw the title, and the screen binds
`useCookingIngredients`. Clear ticks is drawn only while a line of the list is ticked (`view.hasTicks`), because with
none ticked it has nothing to do.

Presentational: props → JSX.

native alike: the house `Sheet` and the list each resolve to their own platform leaf, so this one file serves both.

close route reaches `onClose`, because the host answers by changing `open`.

implementations.name: CookingScaleNote
implementations.moduleDoc:
CookingScaleNote — the web scale note under a step: a muted info glyph and the sentence that says the steps
give amounts for another serving count, in the small muted type that marks it as not part of the step. While the
screen gives it `onOpen`, one quiet button under it opens the ingredients. It holds no state, and it has no live
region because it arrives with the step.

Presentational: props → JSX. The native twin is `CookingScaleNote.native.tsx`, on the same props.
